The Apps

Apps for Learning at Home

Introduce families to helpful digital tools — for reading, homework, creativity, and accessibility.

📱 Real apps, checked to be genuinely free for parents — not an exclusive or ranked list. Two need a library card (free to get — see the Library Card Guide on the Bulletin Board).

Tap an app's icon to see what it does and get the link.

Explore DC

Resources around the city

One of the most important rooms in the Hub — help families find libraries, parks, museums, and other free or low-cost resources around DC.

📍 Real, well-known DC places shown as examples — a full zoomable, filterable map comes later; addresses and hours aren't included yet, so always confirm details before visiting.

Family Resources

Support for the whole family — a resource tree

The little bonsai tree on the desk is this section's doorway — a resource tree connecting families to parenting, academic, food, housing, health, transportation, and financial support, with each branch representing a category.

🌱 A teammate is designing the resource tree itself. Once it's ready, it'll replace this placeholder — categories will be confirmed with Turning the Page staff first.

What's planned

  • A resource tree, with each branch representing a category of support (parenting, academic, food, housing, health, and more)
  • Short descriptions and links or contact info at each branch
  • Categories confirmed with Turning the Page staff before real content goes in
